g.text: Message Queues vs. Pub/Sub — same producer, two different delivery models
Point-to-point queue: each message goes to exactly one competing consumer. Pub/sub: each message goes to every subscriber.
One message, ONE winner among the competing pool — good for "do this job once."
One message, EVERY subscriber gets its own copy — good for "many systems must all react."
ORDERING: a Kafka-style partition preserves order only WITHIN a partition, not across partitions.
Partition by user_id when "this user's events stay in order" matters — cross-user ordering is not guaranteed by default.
ACK TIMING: ack-on-receive can LOSE a message if the consumer crashes mid-process.
ack-on-process-complete can REDELIVER a message if the consumer crashes after finishing but before acking.
Real systems pick at-least-once (ack-on-process-complete) + an idempotent consumer, rather than chasing exactly-once delivery.
